notes: Persistent viral reference library. Kept separate from the production log. Views/medians are the publicly visible counts as indexed by the vidIQ connector on the research date; they change over time. 'why_it_worked' fields are HYPOTHESES, not proven causes. Scene analysis came from vidIQ's short-form video analysis (an AI watch of the public post), not from frame-by-frame human review.

references.creator: @pathlightvisuals
references.topic: Same $10K: buy a car vs buy an income-producing asset
references.hook_0_2s: Split screen on frame 0 with header 'SAME $10K. TWO MOVES.'; coins tossed toward car (top) vs house (bottom)
references.editing_style: 2D stick-figure animation, stacked two-panel comparison, fast beat-synced updates
references.shot_progression: Static locked two-panel frame; outcome diverges inside each panel; header swaps to moral at end
references.typography: Bold geometric uppercase sans, wide tracking, soft glow
references.sound: Music only (electronic beat) + coin/cash-register and dull-thud SFX on each number change
references.payoff: Asset side ends +$11,000 and the car appears anyway; spender's car halves in value
references.performance_evidence: 8.1M views = 334x creator median (strongest relative outlier found)
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: Instant A-vs-B framing needs no explanation; constant number movement holds attention; ~10 s length encourages loops; aspirational moral
references.adaptation_notes: Keep: identical-input A/B split, numbers that move on the beat, header swap ending. Change: no stick figures/characters, no car-vs-house props, original headline wording, honest compound math with visible assumptions, our own palette/type/motion.
references.licensing: Watched for analysis only. No footage, audio, graphics, character designs or text reused.

references.creator: @rovo.stories
references.topic: Same $1,500, same $1,000 emergency, three habits (spend / save / invest)
references.hook_0_2s: Three stacked floors, header 'SAME $1,500. SAME EMERGENCY.'
references.editing_style: 2D animated three-tier split, industrial set, month counter
references.shot_progression: Allocation → emergency slam → months pass with debt compounding vs money tree growing through ceilings
references.typography: Heavy all-caps display with stroke + serif tier labels
references.sound: Upbeat game-like beat, siren on emergency, cash/coin SFX
references.payoff: Investor's tree breaks through the floors above
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: Relatable shock event (emergency) plus 90%/9%/1% identity labels invite self-comparison and comments
references.adaptation_notes: Future episode idea: emergency-fund pillar with a shock event; growth crossing panel borders is a strong visual. Must use honest interest math.

references.creator: @mushinvisuals
references.topic: Pay yourself first vs save what's left
references.hook_0_2s: Header 'Why you can't save.' over two rows of labelled beakers
references.editing_style: Minimal glowing line animation, dark background, warm accent
references.shot_progression: Two rows pour salary into beakers in different order; top runs dry before SAVINGS
references.typography: Clean Inter-like sans, mixed case, one accent word
references.payoff: 'Don't save what's left. Pay yourself first.'
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: Diagnoses a personal pain ('why YOU can't save') and the fix is one rule; calm premium look
references.adaptation_notes: Strong candidate for the Saving pillar: order-of-operations metaphor. Avoid beaker/pitcher imagery and their phrasing.

references.creator: @amberstepsofficial
references.topic: Luxury first vs assets first over 10 years
references.hook_0_2s: Split 'LUXURY FIRST / ASSETS FIRST', YEAR counter starts
references.editing_style: 2D silhouettes, cold vs warm grading per half
references.shot_progression: Year 1→10 ticker; car depreciates/rusts vs house lights up and appreciates; car bought in cash
references.performance_evidence: 1.1M views = 56x median; account had only 844 followers (format, not audience, carried it)
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: Format-driven: A/B + time-lapse. Note: its house appreciation figures are not explained (accuracy risk we will not copy).
references.adaptation_notes: Borrowed principle for DMM-001: losing side drains of colour while the winning side warms. Our numbers must be computed and labelled.

references.creator: @dlf.visuals
references.hook_0_2s: '$10 A DAY is how you end up in a LAMBORGHINI' with car render
references.editing_style: 2D motion graphics + voiceover, odometer counters, exponential line chart
references.shot_progression: Hook → two friends → year 1/10/20/30 milestones → 'last 10 years beat first 20' → payoff → loop
references.sound: Female VO + tech synth groove, ticks on counters
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: Aspirational object + surprising compound number; stating the assumed return on screen builds trust
references.adaptation_notes: Borrowed principle: show money put in vs value as two lines so the gap IS the growth. Too long for 15 s as-is; one idea only.
references.licensing: Analysis only. Includes a branded car image — never reuse brand imagery.

references.creator: @savingjourney_daily
references.topic: Day 82 of a saving journey: a note dropped into a clear acrylic tower
references.hook_0_2s: A note is already sliding into the slot on frame 0. Text 'DAY 82 / MY SAVING JOURNEY / ONE DAY AT A TIME.'
references.main_message: Consistency, one day at a time
references.visual_style: Static high-angle phone shot, bright flat room light, clear acrylic tower with staggered internal shelves
references.typography: Bold rounded uppercase white with dark stroke, top centre
references.sound: Raw ASMR: paper sliding, acrylic clicks on each shelf, a soft landing thud
references.payoff: The note settles flat on the growing stack
references.performance_evidence: 23.8M views = 1,345× the creator's median (largest relative outlier found in two research sessions)
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: Hypnotic, satisfying motion plus tactile sound. Visible accumulation makes saving feel real. The day counter invites following the series. The fixed frame loops seamlessly.
references.adaptation_notes: Used for DMM-002. Kept: a transparent container, one note per day, a day counter, tactile per-note sound, slow then satisfying. Changed: no footage or hands or real currency; a 2.5D glass column drawn in code; a 365-day time-lapse instead of a single day; light that grows with savings (the 'invisible → visible' metaphor); an original headline and moral; computed totals.
references.licensing: Analysed only. No footage, audio, text or currency imagery reused.

references.creator: @giraffe.8206791
references.topic: Day 12 saving journey: $100 notes through a clear shelf tower, then a tap cascade
references.hook_0_2s: A note drops and lands with a satisfying click. 'My saving journey - Day 12'
references.typography: Clean sans, bottom centre, white with shadow
references.sound: Close-mic ASMR, with tap-tap-tap before the cascade
references.pacing: A note every 1.5–2 s, then a 3 s cascade release
references.payoff: A tap releases every shelf: a cascade of notes
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: Tension then release (the cascade); the ASMR mic
references.adaptation_notes: Supporting principle for DMM-002: build tension, then a release (our time-lapse rush into the light bloom).

references.creator: @paulmichaeldepastene
references.topic: Day 46, $5,000 saved: notes zig-zag down a shelf tower
references.hook_0_2s: Starts mid-motion with a note already falling; 'Day 46 / $5,000 / Saved'
references.visual_style: Static wide, full tower in frame
references.payoff: The stack settles; the top clears so the video loops
references.performance_evidence: 1.2M views = 52× the median on an 855-follower account (format-driven)
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: Starting mid-motion means there's no dead first second
references.adaptation_notes: Borrowed for DMM-002: frame 0 already has a note mid-fall, and the counter sits bottom-left beside the column.

references.creator: @spendshiftofficial
references.hook_0_2s: A stacked scale-up of the math as static text over a mundane kitchen shot
references.main_message: Small habits are big numbers that don't feel big
references.payoff: 'It doesn't feel like $78,000, it just feels like Saturday'
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: The gap between how a habit feels and what it adds up to; very short, so people rewatch to re-read
references.adaptation_notes: Future idea (spending pillar). Don't reuse its punchline structure verbatim.

references.creator: @cut.the.noise5
references.topic: Only you can change your life / if not now, then when / day 1→30 growth line
references.hook_0_2s: Word-by-word highlighter reveal on book paper
references.visual_style: Three looks: book paper, a monochrome billboard, a dark grid chart
references.motion_graphics: Word reveals, a snap zoom, an exponential line
references.typography: Serif book type → fashion serif → italic sans
references.sound: Vocal electronic track; text hits on beats
references.payoff: The line rockets off the frame at 'Day 30'
references.performance_evidence: 2.6M views but only 3× a high median (weaker relative evidence)
references.why_it_worked_hypothesis: Beat-synced typography across three distinct looks gives high visual change in 15 s
references.adaptation_notes: Future 'meaningful quote' episode: beat-synced word reveals plus a change of look per line. Our own words only.
references.licensing: Analysed only. Its music track is not licensed for our use.
